# Marimo Studio 0.1.1

Marimo Studio 0.1.1 adds frontend providers, prepared static delivery, and an
integrated agent workflow to custom web views backed by one reactive notebook.
Build reports, applications, and presentations from the same Python data,
controls, and results.

Create a first view and open it beside the notebook:

```console
uvx marimo-studio view create dashboard --target analysis.py
uvx --with marimo-studio marimo edit analysis.py --sandbox
```

Studio opens in **Develop**, with Notebook and Preview side by side. Click
**Source** to edit the view beneath Notebook while keeping Preview visible.

## Frontend projects and live authoring

- Explicit `view.toml` projects with starters for browser-native HTML,
  [React](https://react.dev/) applications,
  [Reveal.js](https://revealjs.com/) presentations, and
  [Svelte](https://svelte.dev/) applications. Install a view provider to add
  another frontend workflow. Vanilla views can reference local CSS and
  JavaScript files directly.
- Source editing for each project's authored documents, with revision checks
  that protect concurrent edits. Arrange and resize Notebook, Source, and
  Preview panes, then return to a saved layout.
- Immutable build artifacts with source-located diagnostics. A failed build
  or presentation replacement keeps the last successful view available.
- Tabs editing the same notebook share its Python kernel, controls, widgets,
  and query parameters while each tab keeps its selected view. Editing control
  can move between tabs, and Studio activation preserves Code Mode.

Views retain native notebook cells, rendered Python objects, controls, widgets,
and browser values through `<marimo-cell>`, `<marimo-output>`, and `mo-value`
projections.

## Prepared static delivery

- **Prepared** (`zero-python`) previews and exports precomputed notebook
  results. Visitors receive the view and captured results while Python source
  stays on the producer. This is the default static export runtime.
- Declare interactive input combinations in `states.yaml`. Controls select a
  prepared state and update its results together. A missing state or failed
  asset load retains the preceding display.
- Run `view preflight` before publishing to inspect projection portability,
  preparation progress, and browser asset references. Export validates the
  staged directory before replacing the destination.
- Choose **Browser** (`wasm`) for visitor-side Python computation through
  [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org/), or **Python** (`server`) for server files,
  packages, and live services. `marimo run` serves Python and Browser views.
  Browser exports include notebook source and run from a static HTTP directory.

See [Run or export a view](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-studio/guide/run-and-share)
for runtime requirements and prepared-state examples.

## Agent authoring and deployment

- Packaged Agent Plugin resources and notebook-bound Python and CLI APIs let
  coding agents inspect, edit, build, show, and validate views. Browser
  validation inspects the rendered presentation attached to the active session.
- [Marimo Lens](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-lens/) connects selections
  in Studio projections to their producing notebook cells for agent feedback.
- Hosts can keep the native Marimo editor at `/` and expose Studio at
  `/studio/` with `MARIMO_STUDIO_EDIT_ROOT=marimo`.
- Exact-origin allowlisting for [embedding the Studio edit
  workspace](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-studio/guide/deploy#embed-the-studio-edit-workspace).
  Same-origin framing remains the default, and Marimo authentication remains
  required.

## Examples and documentation

Nine live views backed by athlete, occupancy, and earthquake notebooks cover
reports, explorers, maps, monitors, model reviews, stories, and presentations.
Each includes source and a guided explanation. The documentation now covers
frontend providers, agent authoring, static delivery, deployment, migration,
and troubleshooting.

## Upgrade from 0.0.6

Marimo Studio 0.1.1 begins the first documented compatibility line. Existing
0.0.6 views need a `view.toml` manifest before Studio can discover them. CLI
automation moves to the `notebook`, `view`, `status`, and `validate` commands,
and Python authoring moves to `marimo_studio.authoring` or
`marimo_studio.agent`.

Static export now defaults to Prepared delivery. Add `--runtime wasm` to
`view export` to retain 0.0.6's browser-side Python execution.

Follow the [0.0.6 upgrade
table](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-studio/reference/compatibility#upgrade-from-006)
before opening an existing workspace with 0.1.1.

## Compatibility

Marimo Studio 0.1.1 supports Python 3.10 through 3.14 and Marimo 0.24.0. React,
Reveal.js, and Svelte authoring use the optional Deno 2.9.5 dependency. Browser
acceptance targets current Chromium on Linux and Windows.

Installed view providers execute trusted Python and child commands with the
current user's permissions. Review provider packages and dependencies before
using them in an environment with credentials or private notebook source.

Read the [documentation](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-studio/),
[compatibility and support policy](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-studio/reference/compatibility),
and [troubleshooting guide](https://marimo-team.github.io/marimo-studio/guide/troubleshooting).

[All changes since 0.0.6](https://github.com/marimo-team/marimo-studio/compare/v0.0.6...v0.1.1)
